GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2013-01-18T19:45:06Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Weird behavior when model.save if option.validate is not set
Description: When validate is not set when calling model.save, it will call 'model.set' in 'model.save' with option passed in, so no validation. Later, option will be extended with {validate : true}, which makes 'model.save' fail. However, since the 'model.set' is done, the data presented wrongly in the view.

I think the behaviors should be consistent, maybe. If no validate: true in option, it doesn't extend the option and check when save.

The problem is that model.set is called without validation, but later the options are extended with {validate: true}, causing model.save to fail while the data is already incorrectly presented in the view. This is a conceptual issue about the flow of validation in the code that can be verified through code analysis without needing to build or run the application. A reviewer can examine the source code of the model.save and model.set methods to verify if the described behavior exists and if the proposed solution (making the behavior consistent by not extending options with validate:true when it wasn't initially set) would resolve the issue.
